chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Najran from Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Allah the Exalted said to His Prophet (peace be upon him): 'O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has made permissible to you, seeking the pleasure of your wives? And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.'
Allah has prescribed for you the expiation for your oaths.
So he made it an oath and expiated it, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him). I said: 'With what did he expiate?' He said: 'He fed ten poor people, for each poor person a mudd.'
We said: 'And whoever finds clothing?' He said: 'A garment that covers his private parts.'

key_terms.مُدٌّ: A specific unit of volume for dry food

ai.seo_question: What is the specific method and quantity for expiating an oath in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's chain elucidates the specific legal details of expiating an oath (kaffarat al-yamin), linking the practice directly to the Quranic verse in Surah Al-Mujadila (65:1) regarding the Prophet's voluntary abstinence. It establishes the hierarchy of expiation methods, prioritizing feeding ten poor people with a mudd of food or providing adequate clothing, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical, accessible acts of charity for oath expiation.
